title: What survives is information
summary: The body could be the Chestplate or an earlier offering. What survives is the Journal and the information it records.

chain.body: The Chestplate, or the physical offerings recorded by the Journal.
chain.gone: The Chestplate is consumed at R1; other offerings are used for earlier steps.
chain.remains: The intact Journal and the recorded answers.
chain.assemble: Reconstruct a message or instruction from authentic entries. No consistent extraction rule has been established.
chain.signal: A unique instruction followed by a Journal advance; neither has been demonstrated at R6.

against: R1 reveals a whole book, not loose pages to assemble.
DEFAG and the letter counts do not by themselves select a decoding rule.
missing: An extraction rule supported by the text, which gives one actionable result without rearranging letters to fit.

title: The event ends; the group remains
summary: Better Together has an ending message about cooperative spirit surviving. Maybe the assembly is people coming together after the festival.

chain.body: The festival as a temporary event. This meaning of body is still an interpretation.
chain.remains: Its ending message describes cooperative spirit surviving; a lasting mechanic has not been shown.
chain.assemble: Players stay or gather together. Where, how many, and whether music matters are not established.
chain.signal: A Journal advance associated with a recorded event transition and group action.

against: Announcement wording is not proof of a retained buff or quest flag.
The clue does not independently specify an event, group size or musical performance.
missing: A clear result for the ending itself, with before/after Journal checks and the actual group action recorded.

title: Rebuild a physical object from the aftermath
summary: A creature or object disappears and leaves materials. Assembly would be a real gathering, conversion or reconstruction interaction.

chain.body: A creature or physical object selected by more than a matching name.
chain.gone: Death, destruction or use of that object.
chain.remains: Identifiable drops or consequences, possibly created by a secondary event.
chain.assemble: Use a documented native interaction to gather or reconstruct them. Chum filling and fossil reconstruction are existing examples, not new discoveries.
chain.signal: A Journal advance at a documented assembly action or final hand-in.

against: Several versions already have reported attempts, including actual acquisition and filling.
A fitting reconstruction mechanic does not tell us which object the clue selects.
missing: A source that selects one particular body and remnant, plus evidence distinguishing its native interaction from recorded attempts.

title: A body is gone, but something nonphysical survives
summary: Spirit, identity, memory or knowledge might be the remainder. This reading needs an actual collection or assembly action before it becomes a solution.

chain.body: A person or creature, possibly the owner of the Chestplate.
chain.gone: Death or loss of physical form.
chain.remains: A spirit, identity, memory or knowledge. None is uniquely selected.
chain.assemble: Unknown. Offering an item named Spirit does not establish an assembly operation.
chain.signal: Unknown until a specific mechanic and completion action can be identified.

against: The Dead Man, Chestplate owner and Journal author have not been shown to be the same person.
Literary connections and spirit-named items do not supply the missing operation.
missing: A direct textual or gameplay link identifying what survives and how players can assemble it.

title: Reconstruct an instrument or its music
summary: The instrument stories offer another way to connect a lost physical form with something players can rebuild or play.

chain.body: An instrument, or the creature from which an instrument is made, depending on the story.
chain.gone: Loss in water or destruction. These are different narratives, not one combined event.
chain.remains: Materials, a surviving instrument or music; the stories do not select one shared remainder.
chain.assemble: Rebuild or play something. No SkyBlock operation is yet selected by the literary parallel.
chain.signal: A Journal advance after the selected reconstruction or performance, once a procedure is justified.

against: Kalevala and Orpheus describe different events; blending them can create a connection neither source makes.
Melody’s Hair playing pitches is real, but its R6 role is not established.
missing: An independent connection from the story to a particular in-game action, rather than a chosen tune or recipe.

title: Change the state of earlier offerings
summary: R6 might ask for a change in what is present rather than a new object. This follows the known distinction between R4 and R5 conditions, but the assembly step is still missing.

chain.body: An existing object or group of offerings.
chain.gone: Consumption, pickup or despawn. These events must be kept separate.
chain.remains: Surviving objects or information about earlier actions.
chain.assemble: Unknown. Repeating an offering sequence is not automatically assembly.
chain.signal: A Journal advance tied to a recorded change in state, not just a disappearance.

against: Different earlier-step rules do not force R6 to use absence.
The despawn procedure lacks an explicit outcome; sound differences are not a validated progress meter.
missing: A concrete assembly operation and an observation separating new arrivals from unchanged survivors.
